title: Urges are waves
body: An urge rises, peaks and falls. For many people the worst of it passes in 15 to 30 minutes if they don't feed it. You don't have to win forever, only until this wave breaks.
tryIt: Open Help and start the 15-minute timer.

title: If-then beats willpower
body: Decide before you're tempted. 'If I'm awake in bed after 11:30, the phone goes to the kitchen.' Pre-made decisions hold up better than in-the-moment ones.
tryIt: Write one if-then for your riskiest hour.

title: H.A.L.T.
body: Urges climb when you're Hungry, Angry, Lonely or Tired. Check which one is true before you do anything else.
tryIt: Eat, message a friend, or sleep. Pick the matching fix.

title: A slip is not a binge
body: The thought 'I've ruined it, might as well continue' does more damage than the slip itself. Stop at one. Leave the room, wash, sleep.
tryIt: After any slip: phone in another room, wudu or shower, bed.

title: Guilt vs shame
body: Guilt says 'I did something wrong.' Shame says 'I am wrong.' Shame tends to drive hiding, and hiding drives repeating. Name the behaviour. Keep your identity out of it.
tryIt: Say: 'That was a behaviour, and I'm changing it.'

title: Environment beats willpower
body: Make the bad path long and the good path short. Filters, the night lock and a charger outside the bedroom do the work while you're tired.
tryIt: Charge your phone outside the bedroom tonight.

title: Night is the danger zone
body: Tiredness drains self-control, and being alone with a phone late is the classic setup. That's why the night lock exists.
tryIt: Be off the phone 30 minutes before the lock starts.

title: Replace, don't just remove
body: An empty slot invites the old habit. Decide what you do at 11 pm instead: read, dhikr, stretch, a call.
tryIt: Pick one replacement and put it in your calendar.

title: Triggers are data
body: Time, place, mood, device. Log your urges for a week and the pattern shows up. Patterns can be fixed; vague guilt can't.
tryIt: Log every urge in Help, even the ones you beat.

title: Move your body
body: Ten minutes of brisk walking or a set of push-ups changes your body state and breaks the urge loop.
tryIt: Next urge: 20 push-ups before anything else.

title: Tell one person
body: Secrecy keeps compulsive habits strong. One trusted person, or a doctor or counsellor, takes a lot of that power away.
tryIt: Choose who you could tell. Start with a professional if that is easier.

title: Sleep is treatment
body: Poor sleep weakens mood control and self-control. A fixed bedtime is one of the cheapest protections you have.
tryIt: Set a bedtime alarm, not only a wake-up alarm.

title: Boredom is a trigger
body: Boredom plus a phone is a loaded situation. Keep a short 'when I'm bored' list of five things so you don't have to invent one under pressure.
tryIt: Write your five on a note.

title: Urge surfing
body: Notice it, name it, breathe: 'This is an urge, a 7 out of 10.' Watch it like weather. You are not obeying weather.
tryIt: Breathe in 4, out 6, ten rounds.

title: Professional help works
body: Compulsive sexual behaviour disorder is recognised in the ICD-11. CBT and ACT are commonly used approaches for compulsive behaviours, and a clinician can also check for anxiety, low mood or ADHD that sometimes sit alongside it.
tryIt: Ask a psychiatrist or clinical psychologist about CBT or ACT for this.

title: Don't test the wall
body: Opening a blocked site 'just to see if it works' is rehearsal, not testing. Treat the filter like a wall, not a puzzle.
tryIt: If you feel the pull to test it, open SOS instead.

title: Count total clean days
body: A 30-day run followed by a slip is still 30 days of real change. Track total clean days and urges survived, not only the current streak.
tryIt: Check your total clean days in Help.

title: The 5-minute rule
body: 'Not now. In 5 minutes.' Then another 5. Delay is a legitimate strategy and it works more often than it should.
tryIt: Next urge: set a 5-minute timer and stand up.

title: Change the room
body: Places carry cues. The bed and the bathroom are common ones. At the first urge, stand up and move to a bright, shared space.
tryIt: Make the living room your fallback spot.

title: Wudu as a reset
body: Wudu changes your physical state and interrupts the scene in your head. Two rakat after it gives the urge nowhere to sit.
tryIt: At the first urge: wudu, then two rakat.

title: Guard the first look
body: The pattern starts earlier than the click, usually in scrolling. That's why social apps have a daily budget.
tryIt: Spend your 30 minutes on purpose, not by drift.

title: Progress, not perfection
body: Weekly question: how many urges did I survive? That number is the one you want to grow, not a perfect record.
tryIt: Check this week's insights in Help.

title: Talk back to the story
body: The urge says 'one look won't matter.' Your history says it does. Write your own history on a card and read it when the urge speaks.
tryIt: Write: 'One look is never one look.'

title: Values over feelings
body: Ask what you want the next week to look like: calmer, focused, proud of your habits. Feelings pass; that picture is the one to steer by.
tryIt: Write three words for who you want to be this month.

title: Sunlight and routine
body: Morning light, regular meals and a fixed wake time steady mood, and steady mood makes urges easier to handle.
tryIt: Get ten minutes of daylight before noon.
